sources.title: The Wing Mechanism Involved in the Courtship of Drosophila
claims_used: Courtship sound accompanies movement of an extended wing.
Measured wing-stroke timing and sound waveforms support mechanical generation by the wing stroke.
sources.implementation_effect: Requires actual wing kinematics as the only endogenous source; no song oscillator.

sources.title: Directional cues in Drosophila melanogaster audition: structure of acoustic flow and inter-antennal velocity differences
claims_used: Drosophila antennae receive the particle-velocity component in the acoustic near field.
Acoustic flow is directional and differs between the bilateral antennae.
sources.implementation_effect: Produces vector particle velocity independently at the two actual antennal anchors.

sources.title: Multi-channel acoustic recording and automated analysis of Drosophila courtship songs
claims_used: Pressure-gradient microphones indirectly measure directional particle velocity.
The idealized nearby point-source particle-velocity magnitude falls rapidly, described as inverse cube.
sources.implementation_effect: Motivates a bounded inverse-cube dipole proxy while keeping its gain explicitly engineered.

sources.title: Distinct sensory representations of wind and near-field sound in the Drosophila brain
claims_used: Different Johnston's-organ populations respond to oscillatory near-field sound and sustained wind-like deflection.
Auditory populations are phasic while wind-sensitive populations can respond tonically.
sources.implementation_effect: Keeps instantaneous bilateral airflow distinct from oscillatory acoustic-band history.

sources.title: Fast intensity adaptation enhances the encoding of sound in Drosophila
claims_used: Sound-sensitive Johnston's-organ neurons respond to fast vibrations in the approximately 100--350 Hz courtship-song range.
Natural near-field sound intensity is treated as air particle velocity and auditory responses adapt to its statistics.
sources.implementation_effect: Supports preserving physical sample history and sub-400-Hz bands without claiming cell-level tuning.
